Color vision
For red-green or blue-yellow color blindness, or seeing no color at all.
Colors for your kind of color vision
Red-green (blue and orange), blue-yellow (teal, pink and red), or no color at all, where brightness and marks carry the meaning.
Marks as well as colors
Debuffs get a letter, item quality gets dots, and threat on nameplates gets a mark ("!" when it is slipping, "!!" when it is lost).
Low vision
For seeing the screen more easily.
High-contrast themes
Pure black panels, white lettering and the strongest rims, in all three families: glass, fantasy and celestial. One button picks the one for the family you use.
Lettering made to be read
Readable (Atkinson Hyperlegible, made for low vision) and Dyslexia-friendly (OpenDyslexic). A thicker outline round every letter, and a dark band behind messages in the middle of the screen.
Bigger text and a bigger interface
Text size and interface scale of their own, separate from the game's.
A ring round your target
A thick outline, 1 to 8 pixels, round your target's nameplate, so it stands out in a crowd. A ring round the mouse pointer too.
Reading aloud
For blind and low-vision players, and for anyone who would rather listen. In the game's own voice.
Talk and quests read as they open
What an NPC says and the choices it offers, a quest's text, its progress and its reward, and books and letters. The reading stops when you close the window.
What you point at
When the mouse rests on something, its tooltip is read aloud. (The game's own screen narrator only works before you log in.)
A key that reads
One key reads the tooltip under the mouse, the quest you are reading, or the last whisper.
Spoken alerts
Ready checks, whispers, missing buffs, loss of control and your own alerts, said aloud.
Hearing
For deaf and hard-of-hearing players, and for playing with the sound off.
Captions for sounds
A line on screen, with a mark for its kind, for ready checks, whispers, queues, invites, duels, resurrections, summons, boss emotes, raid warnings, loot rolls, the aggro warning and your own alerts.
Flashing and motion
For players sensitive to flashing light or movement.
Safe flashing
Nothing flashes more than three times a second, flashes are gentle, pulsing warnings hold still, and the game's red low-health flash is off.
Reduce motion
No fades, pulses, gliding bars or camera drift: things appear and change at once.
A still sky
The celestial themes keep their stars but hold still: no twinkling and no shooting stars, while everything else moves as usual.
Hands and keys
For playing with one hand, or with the keyboard alone.
Keys for one hand

One button puts moving, jumping, targeting, interacting and the first action buttons round W, A, S and D for the left hand, or all on the number pad for the right. Another puts every key back as it was.
The game's windows by keyboard

With an NPC's talk, a quest, a vendor, the mailbox, loot, a trainer, a flight master or a question box open, Tab moves from button to button and Enter presses it, with a ring to show where you are and each choice said aloud if you like.
The settings by keyboard
Tab and the arrow keys go from setting to setting, Space switches one, Left and Right move a slider.
Bigger controls
Larger switches in the settings, and "click twice" buttons wait ten seconds for the second click.
The route planner and gold
New in 13.0: following a route and making gold in the way that suits you.
The planner by keyboard

With Move through the settings with the keyboard on, Tab and the arrow keys go through the planner window, Space or Enter press a button or a switch, and Left and Right change a choice or a slider. In a fight, every key goes back to the game.
Keys for the route
Next step, skip step and plan again can each be bound to a key in the game's key bindings, so a route can be followed without the mouse.
The route read aloud
With Read talk and quests aloud on, each new step is read as you reach it. The first-time tour, and a friend's question to plan together, are read aloud too.
Colors for your eyes
The planner's lists take their colors from your theme and your color-vision setting. The sell hints say Sell now, Hold or Vendor it in words, so color is never the only sign.
Bigger buttons
With Bigger controls in the settings on, the buttons of the planner window, the guide panel and its menus are taller too.
A tour you can skip
The first time, four short pages explain the planner. Skip closes them at once, Left, Right, Enter and Esc work too, and How the planner works opens them again.
The arrow, your way

The planner window's Stop puts the route and its arrow away until you plan again. /fgui move moves the arrow, TomTom's arrow can take its place, and with Reduce motion on it does not pulse when you arrive.
Breaks
With Remind me to take a break at a stopping place on, the route tells you when you reach a good place to stop after a long stretch of play, from 1 to 3 hours as you choose.
Focus and calm
For a quieter screen.
Calm mode
One notification at a time, held for fifteen seconds and put away with a click, and messages that stay up longer.
A wait before tooltips
Tooltips show only when the mouse rests a moment, so sweeping across the screen does not throw one up after another.
Share it
For helping a friend, or setting up a new character.
One line of text
All your accessibility settings as one line to copy, keep or give to someone; pasting it back sets them all at once.
A Comfort step in the setup
The first-time setup has a step for seeing, hearing and calm, so it is ready before you play.

Fantasy Glass UI has accessibility built into every part of the interface: colors for each kind of color vision, high-contrast themes, lettering made to be read, captions, reading aloud, safe flashing, and keys for one hand. All of it is free, and every part can be switched on or off.
In the game: /fgui access opens the Accessibility settings, and the first-time setup has a Comfort step.
What it does not do (yet)
It is not a screen reader: reading aloud covers talk, quests, books, tooltips, whispers and the buttons of the game's main windows, but not every part of every window.
The gold window has no keys of its own yet, and is not read aloud.
The two readable lettering styles have Western European letters only. Reading aloud uses the voices your computer gives the game.
Ideas and problems are welcome on Discord.

Keeping ElvUI

With ElvUI loaded, Fantasy Glass UI steps aside for the parts ElvUI draws: unit and raid frames, action bars, bags and bank, nameplates, the minimap, chat, tooltips and a few bars. Asked often
Which game is it for?
WoW Forever (interface 16001). It goes in World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns, as folders side by side (all of them from the zip).
Does it work with my other add-ons?

Yes. When you already use an add-on that does the same job, like Plater for nameplates, Bagnon or Baganator for bags, or Grid2, VuhDo or Cell for raid frames, Fantasy Glass UI steps aside for that part and keeps everything else. /fgui conflicts off makes it keep its own instead.
Can I use only some of it?
Yes. Every part has its own switch in /fgui, so you can keep the bags and nameplates, say, and leave the rest to the game.
I prefer square frames. Can I get the classic look?
Yes. In /fgui, under Frames and bars, choose Classic instead of Starcut and every frame, bar and button goes back to the box shape, in whichever theme you have.
Does it help with color blindness, low vision or hearing?

Yes, a whole category of it. /fgui access has colors for each kind of color vision, high-contrast themes, lettering made for low vision and for dyslexia, captions for sounds, reading aloud of talk, quests and tooltips, the game's windows by keyboard, keys for one hand, safe flashing, a still sky and a calm mode. Everything it does, need by need, is on the accessibility page.
Will it slow my game down?
Parts you turn off do not run at all. To see for yourself, /fgui perf shows how much time each part takes, /fgui perf fight measures your next fight, and /fgui memory shows its memory.
Something looks wrong. How do I put it back?

/fgui undo puts back your last move or resize, and /fgui history lists what you changed so you can undo any of it. /fgui reset (typed twice) returns the profile to how it came, and a backup is kept first: /fgui backup lists them. /fgui safe reloads with every feature off, to find out whether a problem is ours.
Can I share my setup with a friend?
Yes. /fgui pack puts your whole interface (profile, layout, theme, bars and mail rules) in one string to paste, and /fgui send <name> layout sends it straight to another player who has the add-on.
Where can I get help, or show off my setup?
On our Discord: ask in #fgui-help, post screenshots in #show-your-ui and share theme codes in #themes. Bugs and ideas have their own channels there too.
Which languages does it speak?
English, German, French, Spanish, Russian, Portuguese, Italian, Korean and Chinese. It follows your game's language.
Is it free?
Yes, free, with no ads and nothing to buy.

Common problems
Something looks wrong, or an error appears
Type /fgui check for a report on what is running. Then open /fgui, press Report a problem, and paste what it gives you into a bug report or on Discord.
I can't get into the options, or the screen is broken
/fgui safe reloads with every feature off. Fix what you need in /fgui, then type /fgui safe again to leave safe mode.
I want my old settings back
/fgui backup lists the backups made before each update, once a day and before a reset. Click one to see how to put it back. /fgui history lists single changes, and you can undo any of them.
Panels won't move during a fight
The game does not let any add-on move or resize frames in combat. Wait for the fight to end; equip best and sorting the bags, asked for during a fight, happen by themselves when it ends.
Sending to another player does nothing in a dungeon
Inside dungeons and raids, WoW Forever does not let add-ons send messages to other players. Sending a layout, a theme or a talent build says so there; try again outside.
Buffs look different in combat
On WoW Forever, buffs and debuffs are hidden from add-ons during combat, so the game's own buff frames are restyled and used instead.
A command did nothing, or I can't remember one
/fgui help lists every command in a window you can search. If you mistype one, the add-on suggests the nearest.
“Interface action failed”
Type /fgui blocked and add what it says to a bug report.

Two helpers inside Fantasy Glass UI: a route planner that works out your quests as you level, and Ways to make gold, which lists what is worth your time. Both are free. The planner loads when you use it, and the gold ideas when you use them or open the auction house.

Levelling
The route planner
It works out a route of quests for your level: which to take, in what order, and when to fly, train or hand in. As you play, it plans again, so the route keeps up with you.

The Speed, Safety and Story sliders set what the route goes for. Say how long you can play, and the route takes only what fits and ends at a good place to stop.

New flight points, your class trainer every two levels, a vendor when your bags are nearly full, mail, and a mount reminder from level 40. Each kind of stop can be switched off.

Optional
Questie is optional
The planner works on its own. With the Questie add-on loaded as well, it knows far more of the world.
Without Questie
It plans the quests already in your quest log.
Vendors and mailboxes are the ones you have visited.
Herbs and ore are the ones you have gathered yourself.
With Questie
Every quest at your level, not only the ones in your log, with who gives it and where.
Inns, trainers, vendors and mailboxes, also the ones you have not found yet.
Places to grind when quests run dry, and the goal of finishing a zone, which plans every quest left in it.
In Ways to make gold: which monsters drop the items your quests need.

While Questie is still loading, the planner waits for it, and after half a minute it plans from your quest log. If Questie changes in a way the planner can't read, it says so and plans from your quest log.
Gold
Ways to make gold

One window that lists ways to make gold, best first, from what you have seen: the prices at your auction house, what vendors pay, the monsters you have looted, the herbs and ore you have gathered and the recipes you know.
Right now
At the top, a few things you can do at once, such as selling what is in your bags.
Every kind of idea

Selling your bags, and your bank as you last saw it, vendoring junk, buying from a vendor what sells for more at auction, crafting for profit, gathering loops, monsters worth killing and dungeon drops.
Ranked your way
Each idea says how much it brings, how easy and how sure it is, and how fresh its prices are. Most gold, Easy money and Safe sort the list, or set the Gold an hour, Ease and Safety sliders yourself.

Type an amount, or pick Riding at 40 or Epic riding at 60, and every idea shows how long it would take to get you there.
Go
Go takes you there with the planner's directions. Your levelling route waits, and comes back when the trip ends.

Beside the auction house, Gold ideas here lists what is worth doing there and then. Opening the auction house loads it; Gold ideas at the auction house, under Bags and items › Gold and farming in the settings, switches it off.

How-to
Check you both can

You both need Fantasy Glass UI 13.0 or newer, and there can be no more than 6 levels between you. You need to be friends in the game or on Battle.net, in the same guild, or in the same group: no one else can ask you.
Target your friend
Target them, or be in a party with just the two of you. You can also type /fgui guide duo and their name.
Ask them
Press Plan with a friend in the planner window, under With others, or in the guide panel's menu.
Your friend answers
They see your question with Plan together and No thanks, and have 30 seconds to answer. With reading aloud on, the question is read to them.
Play together
You plan the route, and your friend follows the same quests in the same order. Your panel shows where your friend is, and tells you when to wait for them.
Stop together
Press Stop planning together in the guide panel's menu, or type /fgui guide duo off. Logging out or reloading ends it too.
Good to know
Planning together pauses inside an instance, and goes on when you come out.
If your friend has no Questie, the route plans the quests you both have.
The two add-ons talk only to each other, by whisper. Nothing is written in public chat.
Rather not be asked? Turn off Let friends ask to plan with you in the planner window.

Professions on the route
Training, gathering and crafting for your professions, fitted into the route.
Dungeon runs in the plan
Dungeons at the right level, with their quests, as part of the route.

Dungeons give a lot of experience, so the planner will count them too, for solo players as well. It weighs a dungeon against the quest areas near you, with the time to find a group, get there and run it, and plans one only when it comes out ahead. The dungeon then becomes real steps in your route.
What a dungeon run adds to your route
Pick up the dungeon's quests on the way.
Travel to the entrance.
Find a group. The Find a group button only fills your chat box: you send it. Already in a group of three or more? The step ticks by itself.
Run it. The step ticks when you leave the dungeon after being inside.
Hand in the dungeon's quests.

No group after about 15 minutes? Skip this dungeon plans the rest of your session without it. Planning with a friend, you are already two of the five. A switch in the planner window, Dungeon runs in my route, turns it off, and Keep my route never adds a dungeon by itself. Dungeon runs need Questie.

A speed budget
Tests that stop the add-on from getting any slower.

You won't see this one, and that is the point. Timing tests will measure the add-on's own work and fail when a change makes part of it clearly slower, so it doesn't slowly get heavier. Each limit has plenty of room, so a test fails only on a real slowdown.

Saved-data tidy and backup
Old saved data tidied away, and a backup of your settings kept.

The daily backup, and the one made before an update, will also keep your planner, gold and guide records, and a restore puts them back with the rest. Auction prices are left out, since your next scan brings them back, so the saved file stays small.
Tidying up
/fgui data lists what each part keeps, and roughly how big it is.

/fgui data tidy, or its button in the settings, lists what it would remove: characters not played in 180 days, price scans older than 30 days, leftovers from finished trips and from guides that are gone, and records of guides you deleted.
It asks first. Nothing is removed until you say yes.
Nothing is ever removed by itself. The first time you log in after the update, one line in what's new tells you about it.

Class quests on time
A heads-up before each class quest, so you are ready for it at the right level.

A class quest won't catch you on the wrong side of the world. A level or two before it, you get a heads-up, once in the guide panel and once in chat. When you reach its level, the route goes to where it starts before other far-off places, and does first any quest it needs.
A level 10 class quest that starts in Stormwind, for example
A level or two before: “Your level 10 class quest is coming: it starts in Stormwind.”
The level before: no flight away from it that you would only have to take back.
Level 10: the route goes to Stormwind before other far-off places.
It follows your Plan class quests setting, and a quest on your “Never suggest this quest” list gets no heads-up.
